blocks.text: The explanation of the scripture, in two parts: first, the explanation of the scripture-title; second, the explanation of the scripture-text. The first in two: first, the proper explanation of the title.
The sub-sections, in two parts: first, the general statement.

inline.s: [Commentary] To explain this sutra-title by the five-fold profound meaning: following Master Gushan, take the fruit-person of the two lands as the name, the Vaipulya real-form as the substance, faith, vows, and pure karma as the cardinal purport, the forsaking of suffering and the obtaining of joy as the function, and the Great Vehicle of raw ghee as the doctrinal classification.

[Sub-commentary] 'The five-fold' are name, substance, cardinal purport, function-power, and doctrinal classification. 'Profound' means abstruse and hard to see; 'meaning' means deeply so with a reason. This is the Tiantai Great Master Zhiyi, who deeply entered the Buddha's mind and thoroughly illumined the scripture's intent: before explaining the scripture-text, he first takes that which is abstruse and hard to see, that which is deeply so with a reason, and uses it to explain the scripture-title, so that one who casts a glance at the title at once knows the scripture's meaning. For the name is the scripture's name; the substance is what the scripture-name expresses—the mind-substance of living beings; the cardinal purport is the practice—raising the contemplation-directive from the whole nature-substance and returning the whole contemplation-practice to the cardinal purport of the mind-substance; the function-power is the great function of the scripture's substance and purport in generating goodness and destroying evil; the doctrinal classification clarifies the advancement and the suitability of the Tathagata's teaching in the five periods. The intent is to make students, by the name, seek the mind-substance; by the substance, establish the cardinal purport; by severing doubt, generate faith; by generating goodness, destroy evil; and to know well the great and the small, the one-sided and the round, so that they do not mistakenly confound the scripture's intent.

inline.s: [Commentary] 'The Buddha speaks': Shakyamuni, the teaching-lord, proclaims with the four unobstructed eloquence.

[Sub-commentary] 'Buddha' is the generic title of the supreme sage. To raise his particular title, he is the teaching-lord of the Saha world, fully called Shakyamuni, which here means 'the Able One, the Silent One.' The Able One is his function; the Silent One is his substance. Here the wisdom lies in speaking, which is his teaching-function; hence the substance is set aside and the function followed, and he is titled 'the Able One,' able in his compassion to benefit the three realms. The four unobstructed are: first, unobstructed eloquence in meaning—knowing the meaning-principle of all dharmas, penetrating without obstruction; second, unobstructed eloquence in dharmas—penetrating the names of all dharmas, discriminating without obstruction; third, unobstructed eloquence in expression—for the names and meaning-principles of dharmas, fitting all beings in their different regions and languages, he speaks so that each and all may understand, discriminating without obstruction; fourth, unobstructed eloquence in delight in speaking—fitting the root-natures of all beings and the dharmas they delight to hear, speaking them in perfect accord without obstruction. Whenever the Buddha teaches, he proclaims with these four unobstructed eloquences; hence it is called 'the Buddha speaks.'

blocks.text: Second, the separate explanation of the two characters, in two. First, the explanation of the character 'Buddha.'

inline.s: [Commentary] The Sanskrit 'Buddha' is in Chinese 'the Awakened One,' one of the ten titles. One who has ultimately awakened and realized the real-form of all dharmas is called 'the Perfect Awakening.'

[Sub-commentary] The title calls him 'Buddha'; the Sanskrit is abbreviated, the full form being 'Buddha,' which in Chinese is 'the Awakened One,' belonging to person. If one says only 'Buddha,' the Chinese translation is 'awakening,' belonging to dharma. The generic titles are ten: first, Tathagata; second, Worthy of Offerings; third, Rightly and Universally Knowing; fourth, Perfect in Illuminated Conduct; fifth, Well-departed; sixth, World-knower; seventh, Supreme Person; eighth, Taming Husband; ninth, Teacher of Gods and Humans; tenth, Buddha. Having the ten titles complete, he is honored in the world. 'One who has ultimately awakened and realized' and so on points to the Tiantai six identities; in judging the Buddha, it is the sixth, the ultimate identity, the awakening. The six identities are: first, the awakening of the principle-identity; second, the awakening of the name-identity; third, the awakening of the contemplation-conduct-identity; fourth, the awakening of the semblance-identity; fifth, the awakening of the partial-truth-identity; sixth, the awakening of the ultimate-identity. Because there are six, ordinary beings and sages are not confounded, avoiding the rise of the great pride [of falsely deeming oneself supreme]; because there is identity, beginning and end are not two, avoiding the rise of discouragement. The first, the awakening of the principle-identity: the real-form of all dharmas is perfectly endowed in a single mind; the blind and the dull do not diminish it, and inversion and delusion do not damage it. Hence the verse of Wujizi: 'In movement and stillness the principle is complete; in conduct and in repose all matters are wrong. Darkly one follows things away, and vaguely does not know the return.' This is called the awakening of the principle-identity. The second, the awakening of the name-identity: from a good spiritual friend or from the sutras one hears the names of the three jewels and knows the words of the four truths to be wholly thus, without a hair's difference. Hence Wujizi's verse: 'Just now I heard the song of non-birth; only then did I hear the gatha of deathlessness. Now I know the whole is thus, and regret my former idling.' This is called the awakening of the name-identity. The third, the awakening of the contemplation-conduct-identity: with the whole principle of the three truths one raises the contemplation-practice of the three contemplations, universally subduing the five abodes and entering the station of the five grades. Hence the verse: 'Thought after thought illumines the constant principle; mind after mind stills the dust of falsehood. Universally contemplating the nature of dharmas, there is neither the provisional nor the true.' This is called the awakening of the contemplation-conduct-identity. The fourth, the awakening of the semblance-identity: though not yet formed as a vessel, the coarse defilements first fall away; one sees the semblance-principle and obtains purity of the six faculties. Hence the verse: 'Though the four abodes are first shed, the six dusts are not yet all empty. There is still a film in the eye, and red flowers are seen within the void.' This is called the awakening of the semblance-identity. The fifth, the awakening of the partial-truth-identity: partially breaking ignorance and partially seeing the Buddha-nature, becoming Buddha in the hundred realms and completing the way in the eight appearances. Hence the verse: 'Suddenly the mind opens in understanding; brightly and serenely all is penetrated. Yet the source is not exhausted; one still sees the moon indistinctly.' This is called the awakening of the partial-truth-identity. The sixth, the awakening of the ultimate-identity: ignorance is completely broken and the virtue of the three qualities is fulfilled; tracing the source to the very bottom, one is called the Supreme Person. Hence the verse: 'From of old the true was false; today all falsehood becomes true. One merely revives the original nature, and there is not a single dharma that is new.' This is called the awakening of the ultimate-identity.

blocks.text: Second, the explanation of the character 'Shuo,' in two. First, the glossing explanation.

inline.s: [Commentary] 'Shuo' also means to delight. Meeting the capacity and speaking, it is called the delighting of the Buddha's heart.

[Sub-commentary] Siming says: 'Delight is the flowing delight; the breast is the mind's embrace. To speak of this sutra: it is the Tathagata's long-cultivated and long-realized Buddha-recitation samadhi, stored within his breast. Now that the capacity has knocked and aroused it, in speaking there is the flowing forth of what was formerly held within.'

blocks.text: Second, the distinguishing explanation.

inline.s: [Commentary] Moreover, a sutra may commonly be spoken by five kinds of persons; distinguishing it from the bodhisattvas, gods, sages, and transformed beings, therefore it is said 'the Buddha speaks.'

[Sub-commentary] The five persons can all speak sutras; if they request the Buddha's seal, they may all be handed down. Distinguishing it from the other four, it is therefore marked 'the Buddha speaks.'

blocks.text: Second, the explanation of 'Amitabha,' in two. First, the translation of the Sanskrit.

inline.s: [Commentary] 'Amitabha' here means 'Immeasurable Life.'
[Sub-commentary] The three characters 'Amitabha' are Sanskrit; in this land they are translated 'Immeasurable Life.'

blocks.text: Second, the explanation of the meaning, in two. First, the explanation of 'Immeasurable Life,' in two. First, citing the scripture to explain.

inline.s: [Commentary] The scripture says: 'That Buddha's life-span, and that of his people, are immeasurable and unbounded asamkhyeya kalpas.'

[Sub-commentary] 'That Buddha's life-span' raises the teaching-lord; 'and his people' raises the living beings. In that Pure Land, though there are its people, there is no king. Because its people each take the good as their own rule and need no joint civil and military governance, there is no king; there is only the Buddha as the teaching-lord, the Dharma-king. In general, the life-span of a teaching-lord follows the life-span of the land's people to fix its length. In that land the people's life is still immeasurable; how much more the Buddha's life—could it be measured? This raises the people to reveal the lord: the Buddha's life is immeasurable.

blocks.text: Third, the comparative-superior explanation.

inline.s: [Commentary] Since the response-body is immeasurable, and even the gods and humans do not know its number, how much more the Dharma-body and the Reward-body!

[Sub-commentary] The Dharma, Reward, and Response bodies each have their life-span and measure. Now life is established depending on the life-principle, and the life-principle is sustained by the body. Since the scripture speaks of life and also of body and life-principle, the Tiantai Great Master, in his commentary on the Contemplation Sutra explaining the title 'Immeasurable Life,' illumines the three bodies, three life-principles, and three life-spans, saying: 'The Dharma-body takes the dharma-nature as its teacher-and-rule, and also takes the dharma-nature as its body. This body is neither material form nor mind-intellect, nor is it held within the aggregates, realms, and senses; it forcibly points to the dharma-nature as the Dharma-body. The life of the dharma-nature is not the life-root obtained by retribution, nor does it have a continuous holding; it forcibly points to the unchanging and unmoving as 'life.' This life is neither long life nor short life, neither extended nor shortened; it forcibly points to the dharma-realm as equal to the expanse of empty space. This is the body that is no body, the life that has no life, the measure that is no measure. The Reward body is what cultivation brings about; the Lotus Sutra says it is obtained by long cultivation of karma, and the Nirvana Sutra says the Great Parinirvana is obtained by the practice of the way. The thusness-wisdom illumines the thusness-realm; bodhi-wisdom responds to and merges with the dharma-nature. To respond is like a lid matching its box; to merge is like water and milk merging. The Dharma-body is no body and not-no-body; the wisdom like-wise merging is no body and not-no-body; it forcibly names this wisdom the Reward body. The dharma-life is no life and not-no-life; the wisdom likewise responding and merging is no life and not-no-life; it forcibly names the not-life as life. The dharma-measure is no measure and not-no-measure; the wisdom likewise responding and merging is no measure and not-no-measure; it forcibly names the no-measure as measure. The Response body is the body that responds identically to all things: that which responds identically to the continuous as life; that which responds identically to the long and short as life. When the wisdom is merged with the substance, it can rise to great function, like quicksilver blended with true gold, which can smear over the various forms; merit is blended with the Dharma-body, and everywhere it responds by appearing and going forth. It can be a body and no-body; it can be a constant life and an impermanent life; it can be measureless and can be measured. To be measured has two senses: first, the measure that is measureless; second, the measure that is measured. Such as the seven hundred asamkhyeyas and the eighty years is the measured measure. Such as Amitabha, who truly has a limit yet is beyond the counting of gods and humans, is the measured that is measureless. Responsive Buddhas all have these two measures, following things and conditions, in varying lengths. Yet these three bodies and three lifes cannot be placed side by side as distinct; one-ness or difference would violate the dharma-substance. They are one yet three, three yet one—this accords with the profound text. Now the present text uses the response-life to indicate by comparison the Dharma and the Reward; and on that account the sutra-title is called 'Immeasurable Life.'

blocks.text: Next, the explanation of 'Immeasurable Light,' in two. First, the separate translation.

inline.s: [Commentary] It is also called 'Immeasurable Light.'

blocks.text: Second, citing the scripture.

inline.s: [Commentary] The scripture says: 'That Buddha's light is immeasurable, illumining the lands of the ten directions with no obstruction.'

[Sub-commentary] This too is the light of the response-body of the Immeasurable Life Buddha. Using the light to illustrate the life, the response can likewise be discussed in its three bodies: the Dharma-body is no body and not-no-body, so the Dharma-light is no light and not-no-light, and so on. Now this is the light of the response-body, and yet it is immeasurable, illumining the lands of the ten directions without obstruction—how much more the Dharma and Reward lights!

blocks.text: Second, the explanation in terms of the generic and the particular titles, in two. First, the proper explanation.

inline.s: [Commentary] Moreover, 'Buddha' is the generic title, and 'Amitabha' is the particular title.
[Sub-commentary] All Buddhas have both a generic and a particular title. In the title of this sutra, Shakyamuni raises only the generic, and Amitabha raises only the particular.

blocks.text: Second, resolving the doubt.

inline.s: [Commentary] Shakyamuni is this land's teaching-lord, known to all beings everywhere, so the generic title is raised. Amitabha is the guiding teacher of the Land of Bliss; as a matter of principle he must be manifested, so the particular title is displayed.

[Sub-commentary] Someone may doubt: since the Buddhas have both generic and particular titles, why did the sutra-title not raise the two lands' teaching-lords, generic and particular together, so as to say, 'The Buddha Shakyamuni speaks the Amitabha Buddha Sutra'? Therefore the explanation resolves the doubt: 'Shakyamuni is this land's teaching-lord, whom all living beings have heard and known; so only the generic title is raised, to include its particular. Amitabha is the guiding teacher of the Land of Bliss; if his particular were not manifested, his name would not be shown; so the particular title is displayed, to include its generic.' The translator, to spare repetition and preserve the brief, has fittingly placed it.

blocks.text: Second, the explanation of the generic title, in two. First, the explanation in terms of dharma and constancy.

inline.s: [Commentary] 'Sutra' means dharma and constancy: the ten realms alike follow it, and the three times do not change it.

[Sub-commentary] This explanation of dharma and constancy is drawn from the commentary on the Contemplation Sutra by a transferred explanation, and again from the Miaozong Chao: the Confucian classics, in their exposition, have these two glosses—'the rule of conduct for ten thousand generations,' hence glossed as dharma; 'not changed by a hundred kings,' hence glossed as constancy. The Buddhist sutras are the same: the ten realms all take them as the rule, and the three times do not change them.

blocks.text: Second, the explanation by the reason of the meaning.

inline.s: [Commentary] Because it is proclaimed from the golden mouth of the sage, it is therefore called a sutra.
[Sub-commentary] The Miaozong Chao says: 'Because the Buddha, the great sage, from his golden mouth proclaims the dharma that he himself has realized, it is therefore called a sutra.'

blocks.text: Second, the combined explanation of the generic and the particular, in two. First, pointing to the two names, generic and particular.

inline.s: [Commentary] Moreover, 'sutra' is the generic name, and 'the Buddha speaks' and the rest are particular names.

[Sub-commentary] Miaozong says: 'As to the generic name: whether sudden or gradual sayings, provisorily set up or provisorily opened, apart from the vinaya and the treatises, all are called sutras; hence it is called generic. As to the particular names: the particular forms are many. Here they follow three—person, dharma, and simile: three single, three double, and one complete, forming the seven particular types. The three single are: single person, as in the Amitabha Sutra and so on; single dharma, as in the Mahaparinirvana Sutra and so on; single simile, as in the Brahma-net Sutra and so on. The three double are: person and dharma, as in the Manjusri Asks about Prajna Sutra; dharma and simile, as in the Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma; person and simile, as in the Tathagata's Lion's Roar Sutra. The complete one of person, dharma, and simile is as in the Srimala Lion's Roar Single-Vehicle Great Skillful Means Vaipulya Sutra. With these seven particular names combined with the generic, the whole of the Buddha's teaching is marked out.'

blocks.text: Second, making clear the reason of the generic and the particular, in five. First, the general discussion of a single transformation.

inline.s: [Commentary] The sutra has three kinds: teaching, practice, and principle. Relying on the teaching one cultivates the practice, and from the practice one reveals the principle.

[Sub-commentary] Miaozong says: 'Our school, in explaining the title, discusses it in terms of the generic and the particular because these two names each contain teaching, practice, and principle. Without these three, merely discussing the generic and the particular has no basis. Why? Because relying on the teaching one thereafter cultivates the practice, and from the practice one thereafter reveals the principle.'

blocks.text: Second, pointing separately to the present title.

inline.s: [Commentary] 'Buddha' means awakening; spoken in terms of what cultivation accomplishes, it belongs to practice. 'Speak' is teaching. 'Amitabha' is principle.

[Sub-commentary] In the present title the character 'Buddha' is judged to belong to practice, because 'Buddha' means awakening, which has the sense of self-awakening and awakening others, and awakening and practice both complete. Spoken from the side of cultivation's completion, it belongs to practice. The character 'speak' belongs to teaching, most clearly. 'Amitabha' is judged to belong to principle, because it is the Amitabha of the self-nature: it is precisely as the practitioner, invoking, reciting, and cultivating, that one sees him; therefore it is judged to belong to principle.

blocks.text: Third, judging the generic and the particular.

inline.s: [Commentary] Different from the many scriptures, then the three sutras are all particular. In relation to the character 'sutra,' then the three sutras are all generic.

[Sub-commentary] Different from the many scriptures, then not only do the five characters form the particular, but also the three scriptures of teaching, practice, and principle are all particular. In relation to the character 'sutra,' not only does the single character form the generic, but the three scriptures of teaching, practice, and principle are all generic.

blocks.text: Fourth, concluding as the secret treasury.

inline.s: [Commentary] Principle is the Dharma-body, practice is prajna, teaching is liberation. The three in one perfectly fused and inconceivable are called the secret treasury.

[Sub-commentary] Whenever our school explains a sutra-title, it always does so in terms of the generic and the particular precisely to make clear that each separately contains the three scriptures. And that each separately contains the three scriptures is again precisely to make clear that it contains the secret treasury. As in a single title, the three characters 'Amitabha' are the Dharma-body—the self-nature of me the practitioner; the one character 'Buddha' is the prajna-wisdom that rises to cultivation from the whole nature; the one character 'speak' is the liberation obtained through the wisdom and the Dharma-body. Again, principle is the whole path of suffering as the Dharma-body, the Buddha-nature of the primary cause; practice is the whole delusion as prajna, the Buddha-nature of the illuminating cause; teaching is the whole karma as liberation, the Buddha-nature of the circumstantial cause. These three virtues are like the three dots of the character 'I' or the three eyes of the heavenly king: neither vertical nor horizontal, neither side by side nor separate. They are the inconceivable secret treasury. The meaning-principle of the sutra-title is so subtle. How could teachers and listeners overlook it?

blocks.text: Fifth, concluding as merit.

inline.s: [Commentary] Hence hearing the title-name at the head attains immeasurable merit.
[Sub-commentary] As in the Golden Light sutra and the various Great Vehicles, this is often said.

blocks.text: Second, bringing forth the original name.

inline.s: [Commentary] The original name of this sutra is 'Praise of the Inconceivable Merit, the Sutra Guarded and Recollected by All Buddhas.'

blocks.text: Third, distinguishing the differences in translation, in three. First, the general statement.

inline.s: [Commentary] Handed down to China, there are two translations in all.

blocks.text: Second, the separate statement, in two. First, the Tang translation.

inline.s: [Commentary] The Tang translation says 'The Sutra of the Buddha's Reception of the Praised Pure Land.'

blocks.text: Second, the Qin translation, in two. First, distinguishing its difference from the Tang.

inline.s: [Commentary] The present Qin text conceals and abbreviates the sutra-title; after the Buddhas of the six directions it immediately says, 'You living beings should believe this, and so on.'
[Sub-commentary] The Tang translation retains the original name, while the Qin translation does not, because it is concealed and abbreviated, being placed after the Buddhas of the six directions.

blocks.text: Second, praising the Qin translation's skill.

inline.s: [Commentary] Because this sutra properly shows the method of holding the name, and moreover the holy name of Amitabha is what all beings delight to hear, so by using it to establish the title many people believe and accept it. Hence it is universally observed in all the four seas and circulated without end. Such is the translator's skill.

[Sub-commentary] In general, establishing a name is valued for generating good in beings. Here the good generated is of two kinds: first, this sutra properly shows the method of holding the name; second, the holy name of Amitabha is what all beings delight to hear. Hence, by using it to establish the title, many people believe and accept it. Wherefore the Tang translation lies hidden in the great treasury, unseen and unheard, while the Qin translation is universally observed in the four seas and circulated without end. The translator's skill is trustworthy and has evidence.
